the results obtained for each of the ring systems studied, viz. furan, thiopyran, and pyrroles, have provided a wealth of information concerning the nature of intramolecular interactions and the relative stabilities of various conformers of the molecules concerned.
rotational isomerism is not a general phenomenon in the carbonyl derivatives of furan and pyrrole, whereas in thiophene derivatives, the phenomenon is very common.

the rotational isomerism of carbonyl-containing furans, thiophenes, and pyrroles can be understood and rationalized by reference to the electronic and steric effects of substituents on the heteroatom and by reference to the nature of the carbonyl-containing group.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
rotational isomerism is a general phenomenon in carbonyl derivatives of furan and thiophene, whereas the situation in pyrrole is more complicated.
the presence of a carbonyl group in a heterocyclic ring has a marked influence on the rotational isomerism of substituents attached to the ring.

, in general, the rotational isomers of the carbonyl-containing furans, thiophenes, and pyrroles are more stable when the ring oxygen is involved in hydrogen bonding to the carbonyl oxygen than when the ring sulfur is involved.
The main takeaway from our work is that
rotational isomerism is more prevalent in carbonyl-substituted derivatives of furan and thiophene than previously realized and is often associated with steric interactions between substituent groups.

the rotational isomerism of these compounds is governed by the same principles that apply to analogous derivatives of benzene and other aromatic heterocycles, and the same factors that determine the relative energies of the conformers.
, for most of the systems investigated, the rotational isomerism is controlled mainly by the nature of the ring system and not by that of the substituent.
